Get started

Connect GitHub and open your first repository.

About ByteQuay

ByteQuay is a macOS app for GitHub reviews and local coding agents. Let agents build and guide you, choose how much detail to explore, and merge when you feel confident.

A workspace holds a repository’s work. A task is an agent conversation with its own working copy. App data stays on your Mac; GitHub and model requests use the services you connect.

ByteQuay is pre-1.0. These guides cover the development version; check your release notes for availability.

Get started

  1. Download ByteQuay from GitHub Releases. Open the DMG and drag the app to Applications. Follow your release’s requirements; current builds need macOS 14+ and include Java 25, so no separate JDK installation is required.
  2. Choose Use my GitHub CLI login after running gh auth login, or Connect with token →. The app recommends a classic token with repo and read:user scopes.
  3. Choose Home → Repos you watch → + Watch. Select a repository, check its branch and publication destinations, then Watch repository.
  4. Open Pull requests, select a PR, and inspect WorkBench → Changes.

You can review without an agent. For coding tasks, connect a provider. Change appearance in Settings → Personal → Appearance.

Home and workspaces

Home brings together watched repositories and recent activity. A workspace holds tasks, PRs, work items, commits, and memory.

  • Choose Direct clone to work in the selected repository, or Personal fork to publish through your fork. Review the source, push, and PR destinations before confirming.
  • My PRs shows your open work. Snooze hides a card temporarily; Needs attention collects updates needing a response.
  • Unwatch retires a workspace while keeping local history. Watch again restores it. Delete local data is a separate, confirmed removal.

Plan the day with Today

On working days, after the time you set, Home opens with Today: up to five things worth doing first, each with a reason. An agent picks them from ByteQuay’s records; it never writes to GitHub or starts a task. If ByteQuay was closed at that time, Today is made when you return.

  • Click a row to open its PR, task, issue, ticket, or work item. Hover it for Done or Not today; a row also closes when its work happens.
  • The circular arrow makes the list again. A workspace Home shows only its repository’s rows; Needs attention marks Today rows with a sun.
  • On the last working day, This week looks back at what merged and slipped.
  • Settings → General → Daily agenda sets the time and working days, and can plan around your calendar’s busy times (never event titles).
